summary: Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He founded several Dhagpo centres, serving as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling from circa 1977 to 1997, and taught Shenpen Hookham and Henrik Havlat.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University, he studied under Tokuryu Yamauchi and others. He held professorships at Otani University, Harvard University, and the University of Hamburg, later lecturing at Osaka University.
Genro (1717–1789) was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the post of dai-ichi-za at Myoshin-ji.

Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1934. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1965 to 1983, teaching William M. Bodiford.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He completed his education and PhD at Waseda University, served as an assistant professor at Kokushikan University, and later became professor emeritus at Rissho University.
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and became the dharma heir of Sogaku Harada.
Genzao (d. 1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and received instruction under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. He studied under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, earning degrees from Stockholm and Uppsala universities. He served as dean at Uppsala University and was president of the IAHR.

Geoff Childs is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under Tsetan Chonjore, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Australian National University, and became Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche and earned a PhD from the University of Virginia, later becoming an assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia, a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Oxford and Cambridge, he held academic positions at Newcastle, Lancaster, and Cardiff universities, where he became Emeritus Professor.

Georg August Wallin (1811–1852) was a linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Katedralskolan i Åbo and the University of Helsinki, where he later held a post from circa 1851 to 1852.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt, studied at the University of Tübingen, and served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at Elphinstone College and Deccan College in India before occupying the chair of Indian philology and archaeology at the University of Vienna.

Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1742–1799) was a philosopher and scholar. He studied at the University of Göttingen from 1763 to 1767 and held a post there from circa 1770 to 1799, teaching figures such as Carl Friedrich Gauss.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and others. He served as a professor at the University of Leipzig from 1862 to 1885.

Georg Ebers (1837–1898) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Frederick William University Berlin, and Jena, and later held posts at the University of Jena and the University of Leipzig.

Georg Forster (1754–1794) was a scholar in Indology and natural history who studied at Saint Peter's School. He held professorships at Collegium Carolinum and Vilnius University before working as a librarian and scholar at Mainz.

Georg Freytag (1788–1861) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as a repetent at Göttingen, a sub-librarian at Königsberg, and Professor of Oriental Languages at Bonn.
